purpose: Quantify the airspace-surface, wildlife-separation, thermal-plume, and federal-investment claims in the argument recommending against a data center off the RWY 01L/19R end.

iad_rwy_01L_19R.value: 9,400 ft x 150 ft; RWY 01L threshold elev 296 ft, RWY 19R threshold elev 277 ft
iad_rwy_01L_19R.source: FlightAware KIAD runway 01L/19R (reflecting FAA airport record)
iad_rwy_01L_19R.note: 01C/19C is 11,500 ft; 01L/19R is the runway referenced in the argument.

faa_departure_surface_slope.value: 40:1 (1 ft rise per 40 ft horizontal) departure/takeoff clearance surface
faa_departure_surface_slope.source: FAA AC 150/5300-13B, Airport Design (departure surface); TERPS 40:1 OCS

wildlife_separation.source: FAA AC 150/5200-33 (Hazardous Wildlife Attractants On or Near Airports)

thermal_plume_criterion.jurisdiction: Australia CASA (no equivalent codified FAA numeric threshold)
thermal_plume_criterion.source: CASA Advisory Circular 139.E-02, Plume rise assessments
thermal_plume_criterion.note: Best-available published numeric threshold; used here as a reference anchor, not a US standard.

alsf2_length_ft.value: 2,400 ft (3,000 ft where glideslope < 2.75 deg); lights at 100 ft spacing from threshold outward

data_center_power.backup_generator_unit_MW: 2.25 to 4 per unit, many in parallel
data_center_power.fuel: on-site diesel and/or piped natural gas; some gigawatt-class gas turbines
data_center_power.source: Industry syntheses (C&C Technology Group; Woodstock Power; Mitsubishi Power; USPE Global)

iad_recent_federal_grants.source: FFXnow (Concourse E $41.8M); FAA AIG FY2026 award
iad_recent_federal_grants.note: Recent grants only; cumulative decades-long AIP total not compiled here (requires FAA grant history).

calculations.question: How much vertical clearance does the Part 77 precision approach surface allow at a given distance off the runway end?
assumptions: Surface origin is 200 ft beyond runway end at runway-end elevation (Part 77).
Flat terrain approximation; actual clearance depends on ground elevation under the object.
calculations.takeaway: A 50 ft object reaches the approach surface only ~2,500 ft from the surface origin (~2,700 ft from the runway end). Data-hall roofs plus mechanical/exhaust stacks routinely exceed 50 ft, so 'does not penetrate' is a razor-thin margin, not a comfortable one.
calculations.label: analyst_construction_from_regulatory_slope

calculations.question: Height limit under the 40:1 departure surface off the RWY 19R departure end.
assumptions: 40:1 departure surface begins at the departure end of runway at runway-end elevation.
calculations.takeaway: The departure surface is even more restrictive close in (25 ft at 1,000 ft). A structure sited near the departure end has very little permissible height.
calculations.label: analyst_construction_from_regulatory_slope

calculations.question: At what altitude does an aircraft on a standard 3-degree approach overfly a given distance from the threshold? (Bounds where a thermal plume or light source would intersect the flight path.)
calculations.takeaway: Within ~3,000 ft of the threshold the aircraft is below ~210 ft AGL - the control-critical, least-recoverable band. Any plume rise or glare source near the approach lights intersects the flight path exactly where a pilot has the least margin.
calculations.label: analyst_construction_standard_geometry

calculations.question: How far short of FAA separation guidance is a stormwater retention pond sited adjacent to the runway end?

inputs.actual_ft_estimate: 0 to ~1000 (adjacent to development at runway end)

calculations.takeaway: A wildlife-attracting water feature adjacent to the approach/departure end is not marginally non-compliant - it is inside the innermost few percent of the FAA-recommended 10,000 ft turbine separation, and squarely under the airspace the 5-statute-mile trigger is written to protect.
calculations.label: analyst_construction_actual_distance_needs_site_plan

calculations.question: Order-of-magnitude of the prior federal investment Grant Assurance 29(C) protects.
calculations.takeaway: Just two 2026 federal awards total ~$64M. Decades of AIP/PFC/BIL investment in the airfield and NAVAIDs run far higher; Grant Assurance 29(C) attaches to that stack. Precise cumulative figure requires FAA grant history (operator/FAA data).
calculations.label: documented_floor_not_cumulative_total

sensitivities.C1_object_height: If the parapet-to-tallest-appurtenance height is 70 ft (data-hall + rooftop chillers/stacks), the surface is reached at 3,500 ft from origin, not 2,500 ft - meaning any siting closer than ~3,700 ft from the runway end penetrates.
sensitivities.C3_glidepath: At a 2.75 deg glidepath (flatter, and the case that lengthens ALSF-2 to 3,000 ft) overflight heights drop ~8 percent, putting aircraft even lower over the same ground point.
sensitivities.C4_actual_distance: Even at a generous 2,000 ft actual separation, the pond is still 80 percent inside the 10,000 ft standard.

data_gaps_requiring_operator_input: Data-center site plan: exact structure footprint, parapet and tallest-appurtenance elevations, and ground elevation vs. runway-end elevation (to run a true Part 77 / AC 150/5300-13 penetration test).
On-site generation stack parameters (count, MW, exhaust velocity, temperature, stack height) to run a CASA-style plume-rise model against the 4.3 m/s criterion.
Exact horizontal distance from the stormwater facility to the Air Operations Area and to the approach/departure surfaces.
IAD cumulative federal grant history (AIP + BIL + PFC on airfield/NAVAIDs) for a defensible Grant Assurance 29(C) exposure figure.
The specific approach category per runway end (confirm RWY 01L/19R precision-instrument status driving the 50:1 surface).
